title: How to Create a Guided Learning Assignment With Gemini Notebook and Google Classroom
author: Phillip Alcock
summary: Alcock gives teachers a five-step workflow for combining a free OpenStax textbook chapter with an instructional framework in Gemini Notebook, then turning the result into a Guided Learning assignment in Google Classroom. Students work through three problems, explaining their thinking to Gemini, asking for feedback and completing a short quiz, then answer a final question independently. He grounds the routine in a Google study of more than 300 University of Tokyo statistics students, where the Guided Learning group gained 8.1 percentage points against 5.3, but he is careful to say the study does not prove the same routine works in every classroom. The steps cover building an anchor sheet with a prompt, checking its citations, saving it as a Google Doc, creating the assignment and reviewing student transcripts through Insights. He closes with a testing note that the generated sheet ran long and gave away answers, and that Guided Learning was not available in his Classroom account.
points: Combine one textbook chapter and one learning goal with a framework document in Gemini Notebook to produce a one-page anchor sheet of three progressively harder problems.
Put everything the AI needs in the anchor sheet itself, since Gemini does not use the assignment instructions field as context.
The student routine is explain, ask for a hint-first check, take a two-question quiz, then answer a final question without Gemini's help.
Teachers can review AI summaries and individual chat transcripts in Insights, and should tell students beforehand that conversations can be read.
The cited Tokyo gain (8.1 versus 5.3 points) comes from one half-day university session, so treat it as suggestive rather than proof.
quotes: You can use Gemini Notebook to combine a textbook chapter with an instructional framework, then turn the result into a Guided Learning assignment in Google Classroom.
The group using standard resources improved by 5.3 percentage points between the pre-test and post-test. The group with access to Guided Learning improved by 8.1 percentage points.

Google did not report that a particular two-step prompt caused the result. The study involved university students learning statistics in one half-day session, so it does not establish that the same routine will produce the same gains in every classroom.
For this workflow, choose one chapter and one learning goal. Three problems on a single concept will be easier for students to complete and for you to review.
Open the citations and check that they support the material. Review each problem for accuracy, reading level and fit with your learning goal.

The assignment instructions are for students. Google says Gemini does not use that instructions field as context for the Guided Learning activity, so put any information the AI needs in the anchor sheet itself.
Use the summaries to find questions or misconceptions to investigate, then check the student work and conversations before deciding what to reteach.
Guided Learning was not available in the Classroom account I tested, so I could not verify the attachment and preview steps there. Availability depends on your account and school settings.
